name: PSLE and local-school tuition centres
summary: How expat families evaluate PSLE-focused tuition centres when children enter or consider local schools — subject banding reality, package pressure, and how centres differ from school homework help.
body:
PSLE tuition is a dense market aimed at MOE primary pathways. Some expat families use it after joining local schools; others sample it while deciding between international and local tracks. Centres are not a substitute for understanding whether local school is the right fit.

## What centres sell
- Subject-specific weekly classes (English, Maths, Science, Mother Tongue)
- Holiday intensives and mock exam papers
- Small-group vs large lecture formats
- “Heuristic” maths branding and science practical add-ons

Ask how they diagnose gaps versus racing ahead of school pacing.

## Expat-specific notes
Mother Tongue policies and exemptions matter — confirm your child’s MT code before buying Chinese intensives blindly. If you are still on international curriculum, PSLE centres may misalign until a transfer is real. Transport and evening load on top of CCA can burn kids out.

## How to choose
Trial classes beat year packages. Prefer centres that share marked work samples and teacher stability data. Be sceptical of rank guarantees. For learning differences, ask about differentiation — or choose specialist educational support instead.

## Practical tip
Map the weekly timetable with sleep and family dinners first. One strong subject centre plus school partnership often beats four overlapping brands.
